sources_considered.why: Primary demonstration of generating an instruction-following dataset at substantial scale, with explicit model limitations.
Read the abstract and version history, then used the versioned full paper for exact result passages.
The 2023 paper reports controlled paraphrasing attacks and a retrieval-based defense.

evidence_items.publisher: Stanford Center for Research on Foundation Models
evidence_items.explanation: The researchers generated tens of thousands of instruction-following examples, establishing repeatable production at scale. Their accompanying evaluation and limitations do not establish flawless adherence or universal content quality.

Controlled evaluations show that automated rewriting can make generated text substantially harder to identify without simply destroying its meaning. This directly supports the classifier-evasion reading.

evidence_items.locator: Section 5.3, Is retrieval an effective detector with a large retrieval corpus?
evidence_items.explanation: The same paper demonstrates a defense that compares candidate text against stored model outputs. It limits any stronger interpretation that modification makes detection impossible, but does not negate the demonstrated ability to evade other detectors.
